mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns by 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or the effect size is statistically insignificant in a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration above 2% in PAYEMS signals wage stickiness and reduces labor market flexibility, which is associated with lower S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth exceeds 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when PAYEMS growth exceeds 2%, or the effect is not robust across multiple expansionary wage phases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly HOUST (residential construction) by over 10% in the following 20 days predicts increased future demand for consumer durable goods, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline during such HOUST spikes, or the effect is absent in non-crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) of 3% or more for three consecutive months indicates supply-side strength that precedes S&P 500 20-day forward returns turning positive.
failure_condition: No significant positive return window identified in the 20-day horizon during INDPRO expansion phases.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and UNRATE move in the same direction (both rising or both falling) for 5 consecutive months, the alignment suggests coordinated policy and labor market pressures that drive S&P 500 5-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE show same directional change for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive during such aligned regimes, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in UNRATE below 6% for 3 consecutive months reduces the real wage component of consumer spending, which is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 6% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when UNRATE is below 6%, or the effect is absent in non-recessionary labor regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly surge in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above historical averages of 2% each for the next 20 days is interpreted as dual demand signals that drive S&P 500 20-day positive returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to outperform baseline during such dual surges, or the interaction effect is not robust.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where UNRATE is below 5% and INDPRO is expanding monthly by at least 1% for two months, the combination is expected to lower real interest rates and boost investment, pushing S&P 500 60-day forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and INDPRO increases by at least 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day returns occur in this regime, or the effect is not isolated from other macro variables.
